sentences.text: 1 1.Heard learned advocate Mr.Shrenik R. Jasani for the respondent nos.2 to 4 and learned Assistant Government Pleader Ms.Hetal Patel for the appellant nos.1 and 2.
2.These appeals are filed challenging the common judgment and award passed in LAR case no.882 of 2017 with LAR case No.884 of 2017 dated 8.01.2019.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2422/2023 ORDER DATED: 21/06/2023 undefined 3.The present references have arisen out of the award passed by the Land Acquisition Officer in award No. 33/2008 dated 13/08/2008.

3.1.The brief facts that has given rise to the present land reference are as under:
3.2. The present land acquisition references have been preferred by the claimants under Section.18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (herein after referred to as "the Act"), being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the award dated 13.08.2005 passed by the Land Acquisition Officer, Godhra in award No. 33/2008.
The subject land is situated at village Timba, Ta. Lunawada Dist. Panchmahal (Now Mahisagar), which were required for the purpose of constructing Four Lane highway road from Halol to Shamlaji.
After due verification, the same were sanctioned by the State Government and were sent to the Land Acquisition Officer, Godhra for acquisition proceedings.

3.3. Thereafter, the Land Acquisition Officer started acquisition proceedings and issued a Notification Under Section 4 of the Act in NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2422/2023 ORDER DATED: 21/06/2023 undefined the Government Gazette on 31/01/2008 and, in the news papers- namely "Sandesh" Vadodara edition and "Gujarat Samachar" on 19/01/2008.

3.4. Thereafter, notification u/s. 6 of the Act was published in the Government Gazette on 01/05/2008 and, in the news papers- namely "Lok-satta and Divya-Bhaskar" Vadodara eidition on dated 19/04/2008 and also issued personal as well as public notice u/s. 9 of the Act.

3.5. After considering the relevant facts, the Land Acquisition Officer was pleased to award compensation at Rs.4.50 Ps. per Sq. Mtr. for JARAYAT in Award No. 33/2008 along-with 30% solatium, and benefit of increase of 12% on compensation amount.
3.6. Thereafter, the notices were served to the interested parties and they were also given opportunity of being heard.

Ultimately, the Land Acquisition Officer was pleased to deliver the award No. 33/2008 on 13/08/2008 wherein, the claimants were awarded Rs.45,000/- per hectare for agricultural land as the market value of the acquired land, along-with 30% solatium and benefit of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2422/2023 ORDER DATED: 21/06/2023 undefined increase of 12% on compensation amount.

The details of the acquired land for these references are as under:
Village Timba, Tal. Lunawada, Dist. Panchmahals Sr. No. L.A.R.No. Survey No. Area of land acquired (Hec.-Are.-Sq.
Mtr.) 1 882/2017 55 paiki 1 00-04-05 2 884/2017 51 00-01-50 50 00-13-20 3 885/2017 57 00-19-24 4.The land owners preferred the reference under Section 18 of the Act being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the aforesaid award for enhancement of compensation at the rate of Rs.5000/- per square meter.

5. The learned Judge after considering the reply of the opponent and evidence produced before the Court relied upon the award in LAR No.51 of 2010 pertaining to the adjoining village for the same project wherein the award was made at Rs.558/-
per square meter, as against compensation at Rs.6/- per square meter.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2422/2023 ORDER DATED: 21/06/2023 undefined

6. Learned AGP Ms.Patel reiterated the contention raised before the Court below that as the villages are different, it should not be taken for granted that both the land possess the same fertility and potential value and therefore, such award could not have been relied upon by the Court.

7.However, the learned Judge after considering the fact that there is no evidence on record to point out that the fertility and potentiality of the land in the LAR No.51 of 2010 and the facts in the present case being different, came to the conclusion that considering the fact that the date of issuance of notice under Section 4 of the Act was published in LAR No.51 of 2010 on 24.01.2008,
whereas in the present case the notice was published on 31.01.2008.
It was therefore observed that there is difference of only one week between two notices.

The learned Judge has further observed that the total market value of the land in LAR No.51 of 2010 has been determined at Rs.564/- per square meter and in the present case at Rs.4.50 per square meters has been awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer and therefore NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2422/2023 ORDER DATED:
21/06/2023 undefined the difference of Rs.559.50 is rounded as Rs.560/- per square meters and accordingly, awarded further enhanced amount of Rs.560/- per square meter with consequential solatium and the interest.
8.
On a query raised by this Court, learned AGP has candidly submitted that no First Appeal is pending against award passed in the LAR No.51 of 2010 and it has become final.

9.Considering the above facts, no interference is called for in the impugned judgment and award as the subject land of the LAR No.51 of 2010 and the subject land of present reference are situated near by and therefore the learned Judge cannot be said to have committed any error while relying upon the award passed in LAR No.51 of 2010.
Both the Appeals therefore being devoid of any merit are summarily dismissed.
Rule is discharged.
